themes_detail.label: Street Deterioration Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints spiked to 138 this week—a 395% surge from the 27.9-week average—signaling a major deterioration event in Woodhaven/Richmond Hill that demands immediate investigation into whether potholes, flooding, or infrastructure failure is affecting transit and safety.
evidence: 138 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 27.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 16.77, +395%)
This is the single largest spike across all complaint categories in the dataset, indicating acute infrastructure failure
Timing aligns with recent weather or construction activity—requires on-the-ground verification
reporting_angles: Canvass affected blocks to document what specific street damage (potholes, sinkholes, flooding) triggered complaints and affects residents daily
Interview DOT or local city officials about emergency response and whether this signals a broader infrastructure maintenance gap in the district

themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Complaints Explode
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints jumped to 10 this week—a 1233% spike from the 0.8 weekly baseline—suggesting a sudden surge in Uber/Lyft-related congestion, illegal parking, or traffic issues in the neighborhood.
evidence: 10 for-hire vehicle complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 11.16, +1233%)
Second-largest spike in absolute z-score magnitude, indicating a genuine anomaly
Nature of complaints unclear from dataset—requires specificity on whether issue is illegal pickups, double-parking, or driver behavior
reporting_angles: Contact residents and local business owners to learn what specific for-hire vehicle behaviors (illegal parking, blocking fire hydrants, congestion) triggered the surge
Interview TLC or local precinct to determine if there's been a change in enforcement or an influx of drivers targeting this district

themes_detail.label: Noise Surge from Streets and Sidewalks
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints jumped to 17 this week—a 157% increase from the 6.6-week average—indicating a new or intensifying source of disruptive noise (construction, vendor activity, or street performers) affecting resident quality of life.
evidence: 17 street/sidewalk noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 6.6 weekly average (z-score: 3.93, +157%)
Timing aligns with street condition spike—possible construction-related noise
Long-standing category issue: residential noise remains in top-10 complaint types (880 complaints over 90 days)
reporting_angles: Identify the specific source of the noise spike—check for active construction permits, street fairs, or commercial activity in affected blocks
Interview residents about sleep disruption and quality-of-life impact, particularly if tied to infrastructure repair work

themes_detail.label: Rodent Problem Emerging
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints spiked to 6 this week—a 433% surge from the 1.1 weekly baseline—suggesting emerging infestation or sanitation breakdown in Woodhaven/Richmond Hill.
evidence: 6 rodent complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly average (z-score: 4.63, +433%)
Unsanitary condition complaints (250 over 90 days) suggest broader sanitation issues in district
May be seasonal pattern or indicator of waste management failure
reporting_angles: Walk complaint hotspots to assess garbage management, construction debris, and food vendor practices that may attract rodents
Interview DSNY and health department about whether they've detected a spike and what residents should do to report ongoing infestations

themes_detail.label: Cannabis Retail Complaints Spike (2 weeks ago)
themes_detail.summary: Cannabis retailer complaints surged to 9 two weeks ago—a 500% spike from the 1.5 weekly baseline—indicating resident pushback on illegal dispensaries or concerns about licensed retailers' operations in Woodhaven/Richmond Hill.
evidence: 9 cannabis retailer complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 1.5 weekly average (z-score: 5.67, +500%)
Spike timing suggests concentrated period of resident concern—may indicate illegal shop opening or enforcement action
Data does not specify whether complaints target illegal or legal retail operations
reporting_angles: Map where these retail complaints are concentrated geographically to identify problem storefronts or clusters
Interview residents and community board members about whether concerns relate to unlicensed dispensaries, youth access, or quality-of-life impacts
